executiveSummary: GreenPack Manufacturing GmbH, a packaging manufacturer based in Cologne, Germany, reports its ESG performance for the 2025 reporting year. With a workforce of 180 employees, the company achieved a 91% waste recycling rate and sourced 45% of its electricity from renewable sources. Total emissions (Scopes 1, 2, and 3) amounted to 4,300 tCO2e, verified by TÜV Rheinland, with an emissions intensity of 15.5 tCO2e per employee for Scopes 1 and 2. The company maintains strong governance with annual supplier screenings, a Supplier Code of Conduct, and oversight by the Managing Director.

scope1.value: 600 tCO2e (Sources: company fleet and natural gas boilers)

scope3.value: 1500 tCO2e (Sources: supplier transport and raw material production)

findings: GreenPack’s emissions intensity is 15.5 tCO2e per employee (Scopes 1+2).
Renewable energy share of 45% reduced Scope 2 emissions by approximately 1,000 tCO2e compared to the full grid mix.
Biodiversity assessment shows limited impacts as the industrial site has no nearby protected habitats, and biodiversity expectations are established for suppliers.
The company achieved a 91% waste recycling rate, against a target of 95%. Circular economy initiatives include packaging redesign, use of recycled cardboard, and waste reduction initiatives.
A total of 5 supplier ESG audits were conducted, with annual screenings and questionnaires implemented for 120 suppliers.
The workforce consists of 180 employees (160 permanent, 20 temporary; 112 male, 68 female).
There were 2 workplace accidents and 1,240 total training hours completed.
The Managing Director acts as the approval authority for ESG policies, which undergo annual reviews.
Emissions methodology follows GHG Protocol standards, using emission factors from the German Environment Agency (UBA, 2025).
Electricity consumption was 3,200 MWh (45% renewable, 55% non-renewable) provided by Stadtwerke Köln, with Q2 2026 costs totaling 391,300 EUR.
recommendations: Implement planned supplier data collection for Scope 3 emissions.
Achieve the 95% recycling target through packaging redesign and waste reduction initiatives.
Establish tracking and reporting mechanisms for natural gas consumption.
Establish tracking and reporting mechanisms for water consumption.
Conduct a formal data protection assessment and implement data protection policies.
Develop and implement a formal anti-corruption policy.
